patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient has been experiencing tingling pain in the sole of his right foot for the last 6 weeks, which occurs when he raises his foot above chest level during exercises. He started exercising regularly 2 months ago and notices his right calf cramps when using the incline feature on his treadmill, requiring him to stop frequently. The pain subsides after a few minutes of rest. He has been managing type 2 diabetes mellitus for 8 years. He is a smoker with a 34-year history of smoking two packs per day.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate a 55-year-old man presenting with foot pain and cramping during exercise, and diagnose the underlying condition.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I’m your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: For the past six weeks I’ve had a tingling pain in the sole of my right foot when I raise my foot above chest level during exercise. Also, when I use the incline on the treadmill my right calf cramps and I have to stop, but the pain eases after a few minutes of rest.
How old are you, and do you have any medical conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, or high cholesterol?

I’m 55 years old, and I have type 2 diabetes that I’ve been managing with metformin for the past 8 years. I don’t have high blood pressure that I know of, and I’m also a long-time smoker—about two packs a day for 34 years.
Do you ever get this foot pain at night when you are lying flat in bed, and have you noticed any sores, slow-healing wounds, or color changes on your right foot or toes?

Patient: I don’t notice the foot pain much at night when I’m lying flat, but I have seen some color change in my right toes and I’m worried about a couple of areas that seem slow to heal. I haven’t had any obvious new sores.
Have you noticed if your right foot feels colder to the touch
Patient: Yes, the right foot does seem a bit cooler to the touch compared with the left, especially when I’ve been exercising.

Patient: Yes, the right foot is noticeably cooler than the left, especially after I start exercising. I also feel the tingling in the sole mainly during that raising-the-foot motion, and my right calf cramps on the treadmill incline before I have to stop. I’ve noticed some toe color changes and a couple of spots that seem to heal slowly, but no fresh open sores.
